channel.title: Symbol Shelter | Konpo Studio
channel.description: Rejected logo marks by Konpo Studio, catalogued and up for adoption. New intakes as they arrive.

item.title: Lantern (SYM-096)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO NOSTALGIC. Nested meridians swelling to a sphere, drawn twice and mirrored, with every rib meeting at the poles. A wireframe globe that holds up at small sizes.

item.title: Turbine (SYM-095)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO AMBITIOUS. A sliced orb with fins stepping off both hemispheres in even increments toward the poles. It looks like it should spin.

item.title: Marigold (SYM-094)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO WARM. Eight lobes and a core cut from one piece. Built like a rubber stamp, and it holds up at any size.

item.title: Anemone (SYM-093)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO WHOLESOME. Eight petals drawn in one heavy contour of constant weight. Sturdy enough to live on an outdoor sign.

item.title: Warp (SYM-090)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO PLAYFUL. Two strokes woven into peaks, over, under, over. The line weight stays constant through every crossing.

item.title: Cradle (SYM-089)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO GENTLE. A dome settling into its rim, caught one frame before contact. Close the gap and it becomes a bowl.

item.title: Latitude (SYM-086)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO OPTIMISTIC. Horizontal ellipses stacked into a globe, compressing toward the poles at true projection. The horizontal sibling of Meridian.

item.title: Tally (SYM-085)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO COMPETITIVE. Counters in framed cells, like a scorecard. The grid comes first and the dots fill it in.

item.title: Waveform (SYM-084)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO TALKATIVE. Vertical strokes swelling to an ellipse, like a sound wave on a screen. The outline is symmetric top to bottom.

item.title: Aperture (SYM-083)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO WATCHFUL. A ring, a lid and a pupil, like a lens caught mid-blink. The bar sits exactly on the horizontal axis.

item.title: Ripple (SYM-082)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO SOFT. Rings inside rings, weighted low in the frame, spreading out from where a drop landed. They fade toward the edge the way real ripples do.

item.title: Lune (SYM-081)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO FRUITY. Crescent slivers nested inside an O. A lune is geometry’s word for a moon shape. The client said banana.

item.title: Windrose (SYM-080)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO ADVENTUROUS. Spokes tipped with direction markers, set at true intervals. A compass rose without the map, so north is wherever you hang it.

item.title: Daisy (SYM-079)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO INNOCENT. Six outline petals around an open center, their roots sharing one circle. The everyday lawn flower, drafted properly.

item.title: Helm (SYM-078)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO HEROIC. A dome with a low band and curls at the sides. Some saw a helmet, some saw a kettle, and it was never settled.

item.title: Louver (SYM-077)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO LOUD. Horizontal slats filling a softened square. The gap between slats matches the slat height, so the rhythm stays even.

item.title: Dune (SYM-075)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO CALM. A solid dome settling past its baseline, like sand after the wind drops. The flat bottom is where the mass came to rest.

item.title: Knot (SYM-074)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO COMPLICATED. One continuous line looping through four lobes, with no start and no end. Trace it with a finger and you come back to where you began.

item.title: Quartet (SYM-073)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO ORDERLY. Four dashed rings, tangent in a 2×2. The dashes line up at every meeting point, which took an afternoon.

item.title: Coil (SYM-072)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO TENSE. Nested arcs wound into a sphere with a twist at the equator. It looks like a spring, compressed and ready to go.

item.title: Phases (SYM-069)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO MOODY. Crescents overlapping left to right, a month of moon phases in one lockup. Each phase covers part of the one before it.

item.title: Cloister (SYM-068)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO QUIET. Four corner arcs around an empty courtyard. Close the gaps between them and it becomes a plain frame.

item.title: Barcode (SYM-067)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO SALESY. Vertical bars packed into an ellipse. The bars stay evenly spaced and the outline does the curving.

item.title: Stitch (SYM-062)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO CRAFTY. A cross built from square counters on a strict grid, like cross-stitch. Zoom in and it never gets smoother.

item.title: Union (SYM-061)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO ENTERPRISE. Two open rings joined at the seam, their gaps facing away from each other. A merger that actually closed.

item.title: Whorl (SYM-059)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO HYPNOTIC. Concentric ellipses packed until they start to vibrate. The spacing is optically corrected, which only makes it worse.

item.title: Venn (SYM-058)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO CORPORATE. Two circles and their intersection, no labels. The overlap is set at exactly one third. Every strategy deck has one.

item.title: Orbit (SYM-056)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO RETRO. Three ellipses sharing a nucleus, drawn with a loose hand. The atom before anyone wrote a standards manual for it.

item.title: Visor (SYM-055)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO DOMESTIC. An orb with two curved lines low on its face. From across the room it’s a helmet, up close it’s a kettle.

item.title: Tether (SYM-053)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO COMMITTED. Two C shapes hooked into each other, like a chain link with serifs. Pull either end and the counters close tighter.

item.title: Meridian (SYM-052)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO GLOBAL. A sphere sliced by longitudes that thin toward the poles. A globe without the map.

item.title: Dahlia (SYM-050)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO SWEET. Eight solid petals around a core dot, press-fit with no overlaps. Simple enough to cut as a stamping die. Would survive a keychain.

item.title: Argyle (SYM-049)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO OLD MONEY. A lens filled with diagonal checkers at forty-five degrees, like an argyle sweater. The counters shrink toward the tips. Grandfather-approved.

item.title: Garland (SYM-048)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO BUBBLY. Six small rings strung around a seventh, each one touching its neighbors at a single tangent point. Half molecule, half party decoration.

item.title: Synapse (SYM-046)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO SMART. Four pill shapes pointing at a center that isn’t drawn. The empty middle is where the signal would jump.

item.title: Duplex (SYM-045)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO SUBURBAN. Half square, half circle, joined into one silhouette along a dead-straight wall. A duplex with two very different tenants.

item.title: Gyre (SYM-044)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO DIZZY. Two comma shapes chasing each other around a still center. Nothing moves, but the eye keeps turning it anyway.

item.title: Tangent (SYM-043)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO NEUTRAL. A square and a circle that touch at exactly one point. Neither shape gives way to the other.

item.title: Medallion (SYM-042)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO ROYAL. Rings, petals and a rounded frame, every band sharing the same center point. The formal one of the set, made for embossing.

item.title: Parquet (SYM-041)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO GROUNDED. Dot-and-tile pairs in a 2×2 rotation, laid out like parquet flooring. Rotate any unit 90° and the pattern still lines up.

item.title: Circuit (SYM-040)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO TECHY. Paired dots and pills stepping up the diagonal, corner to corner. It reads like a small piece of circuit board.

item.title: Relay (SYM-039)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO FAST. Two pointed nodes flanking a dot, like a signal caught mid-pass. The taper sets the direction, left to right.

item.title: Clover (SYM-038)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO LUCKY. A disc split into four petals that meet at the center. The cross cut between them is the first thing you see.

item.title: Molecule (SYM-035)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO CLINICAL. Dots and bonds laid on one axis, like a compound diagrammed in plan view. Every interval is a multiple of the dot radius.

item.title: Socket (SYM-030)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO STARTUPY. A disc with its core exposed and one channel leading out. It looks like something used to plug in here.

item.title: Rosette (SYM-029)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO FESTIVE. Four rings pinched around a square center. The dashes hold it together. Remove one and the square disappears.

item.title: Hexad (SYM-028)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO SERIOUS. Six wedges locked into a hexagon, meeting at a pinpoint center. The gaps between them are what make it read as six.

item.title: Casement (SYM-027)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO HOPEFUL. Four rounded panes split by a hairline mullion, with matching radii at every corner. A window with nothing behind it yet.

item.title: Bloom (SYM-026)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO HAPPY. A ring of eight dots crowding a clustered core, the spacing tightening toward the middle like a real bouquet. The client called it too happy, which is hard to argue with.

item.title: Corolla (SYM-024)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO POLITE. Five petal-rings around an open center, pitched at 72°. Each ring shares an edge with its neighbor. Drawn entirely with a compass.

item.title: Enso (SYM-023)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO SPIRITUAL. One stroke, almost closed, thinning where the brush lifts. The most hand-drawn mark in a catalogue built with compasses.

item.title: Swarm (SYM-022)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO TIMELESS. Seven equal dots in a loose hexagonal formation. Regular enough to look planned, loose enough to look like it could move.

item.title: Domino (SYM-021)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO CASUAL. Two upright tiles, four counters and one connecting bar. Game pieces that could pass for a system diagram. The pips sit on the grid.

item.title: Binary (SYM-020)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO DECISIVE. Two discs sharing one edge, drawn as a single mass. One reads full, the other is clipped where they meet.

item.title: Asterisk (SYM-019)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO LEGAL. Six serifed spokes off a common hub at even intervals, tips flared like type. A footnote mark drawn at headline size.

item.title: Iris (SYM-018)
item.description: Pictorial · REJECTED · TOO TEARY. A ring holding five vertical lenses, widest at the axis. Half the room saw an eye, the other half saw an onion cut in half.

item.title: Facet (SYM-017)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO EXPENSIVE. A ring milled into eight flats, with no curves left. The two halves stop just short of touching at the waist. An O cut like a gemstone.

item.title: Duet (SYM-016)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO ROMANTIC. Two open rings, each broken where the other passes through. Same radius, same weight, with the openings on opposite sides. It reads as a handshake.

item.title: Tessera (SYM-015)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO MODERN. A circle-packing tile. One full circle at center, part-circles on every edge of the 90u frame, all sharing the same R 21.4. Repeat it and it tiles clean.

item.title: Trinode (SYM-014)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO SCIENTIFIC. Three R 12.6 nodes joined by one continuous bond. The top pair sits 54.2u apart and the apex closes at exactly 90 degrees. A molecule diagram that could pass for a monogram.

item.title: Quatre (SYM-013)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO EDGY. Four R 15 circles set at 90 degrees, each with its own keyhole. A strict compass layout with a playful streak.

item.title: Pentad (SYM-012)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO DECORATIVE. Five arms on a 72 degree pitch around a 25.6u orbit. The symmetry is pentagonal, but there is no pentagon drawn anywhere.

item.title: G Mark (SYM-011)
item.description: Monogram · REJECTED · TOO OBVIOUS. Built on one R 36 circle. The counter is a separate 13.4 circle snapped inside the curve, and the terminal is cut flat against the frame edge.

item.title: Link (SYM-010)
item.description: Abstract · REJECTED · TOO FRIENDLY. Two identical hooks with an R 19 curve, one rotated 180 degrees around the center point so the pair interlocks.

item.title: Rotor (SYM-007)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO BUSY. Two rings and two squares rotated into a single rotor. The arcs use R 40 and R 28.9 from one shared center, and the squares each carry a deliberate 1 degree tilt, set 180 degrees apart.

item.title: Dial (SYM-006)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO FLOWERY. Four R 15 circles locked to the axes on a 30u pitch, each one hatched differently. It reads a bit like the gauges on an instrument panel.

item.title: Ribbon C (SYM-005)
item.description: Monogram · REJECTED · TOO CLEVER. One folded plane inside a 72 by 80 frame, creased at 53 degrees to make the C.

item.title: Bracket (SYM-004)
item.description: Monogram · REJECTED · TOO INDUSTRIAL. Two 24u blocks and a hooked spine with a 12u radius. Part letterform, part bracket hardware.

item.title: Junction (SYM-002)
item.description: Geometric · REJECTED · TOO MUNICIPAL. Four quarter arcs, each anchored on a corner point, with bars splitting the middle at 6.7u. From above it looks like a highway interchange.

item.title: CO Monogram (SYM-001)
item.description: Monogram · REJECTED · TOO CONFIDENT. Two letters built from four radii. The C runs R 36 outside and R 24 inside, the O uses 23 and 12, and the whole lockup sits on one baseline.
